MemeDef.label: Color hierarchy
MemeDef.description: The Colors are not a policy. They are a fact of biology, arrived at by better minds than ours, and a person's worth is settled at conception. Golds rule because Golds are built to rule. Reds dig because Reds are built to dig. To resent the arrangement is to resent arithmetic.

rulesStrings.li: creation(tag=meme_RR_ColorHierarchy) ->[deity0_name] set each kind of person to the task they were shaped for, and called the arrangement good.
episode(uses=1,tag=meme_RR_ColorHierarchy) ->[deity0_name] said: a hand is not lesser than an eye for being a hand, and neither may take the other's place.
setup(tag=meme_RR_ColorHierarchy) ->[founderName] held that a society of equals is a society of no one doing anything well, and set about sorting people into what they were for.
archistFact(tag=meme_RR_ColorHierarchy) ->The great machines sorted humanity once, correctly, and it is not our place to re-sort it.

MemeDef.label: Color equality
MemeDef.description: Somebody decided which of us would be strong and which of us would be short-lived, and then called the result nature. It was not nature. It was a decision, made by people, for their own convenience, and a decision can be unmade.\n\nWhat a person was built for is not what a person is for.

rulesStrings.li: creation(tag=meme_RR_ColorEquality) ->[deity0_name] made one kind of person, and everything that came after was done by hands, in workshops, for money.
episode(uses=1,tag=meme_RR_ColorEquality) ->[deity0_name] asked who had given them the right to decide, and no one present could answer.
setup(tag=meme_RR_ColorEquality) ->[founderName] came up out of the mines, saw what the sorting had cost, and decided it would be undone or they would die trying.
archistFact(tag=meme_RR_ColorEquality) ->Even the great machines never presumed to rank a person by their making.
